page: Vultr vcg-a40-8c-40g-16vram is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance featuring a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 8 shared vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 40.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside 740 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard CPU and memory operations, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14175.12 and a PassMark CPU score of 14090.9. The memory subsystem delivers a read-only large-block bandwidth of 88.57 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 52.63 GB/sec. However, the instance excels in GPU-driven workloads, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference benchmarks. For a small 135M model, it processes prompts at 9944.32 tokens/sec and generates text at 464.42 tokens/sec. For a medium 7B model, it maintains top-tier speeds with 3147.67 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 107.73 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a resource-density perspective, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU acceleration by utilizing a fractional GPU allocation. This allows users to access 16 GB of VRAM without paying for a full dedicated GPU. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and a moderate 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits raw single-core CPU performance, as shown by the average stress-ng single-core score of 1786.68.

This configuration is highly suited for small to medium large language model inference, machine learning prototyping, and data science tasks that require GPU acceleration but do not demand a full dedicated card. It is also appropriate for database operations, as evidenced by its 14.91 million operations/sec in Redis SET benchmarks, and general-purpose workloads requiring fast local NVMe storage.
